introduction-the-centralization-trap.core: Traditional ML copies all data to a central server, which is often impossible because of privacy law (GDPR, HIPAA), bandwidth or competitive concerns. Federated Learning flips it: send the model to where the data lives, train locally, and share only model updates.

first_principles.problem: Hospitals want a joint diagnostic model but cannot legally pool patient records.
truths: Data may be legally or physically immovable.
Models are much smaller than datasets.

analogy.title: Researchers visiting libraries instead of moving the books
analogy.story: The books stay where they are; the researchers bring back their notes.
analogy.breaks: Notes can reveal more than you think, since gradients can leak data without extra protection.

example.title: Hospital consortium
flow: Server sends global model to 5 hospitals

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A shared model without sharing records.

check.q: What moves in federated learning: data or model?
check.a: The model (and its updates); raw data never leaves the client.

the-algorithm-how-fedavg-works.core: Federated Averaging: each round, the server samples clients, sends the global weights, each client runs several local SGD epochs, and the server averages the returned weights weighted by each client's sample count. Multiple local steps cut communication rounds.

first_principles.problem: Sending gradients after every batch from millions of phones is impossibly chatty.
truths: Communication is the bottleneck, not compute.
Local steps make progress without talking.

analogy.title: A group project where everyone drafts at home
analogy.story: Each person works on their copy, then the editor merges drafts, giving more weight to bigger contributions.
analogy.breaks: Drafts can be merged by judgement; FedAvg averages numbers blindly, which hurts if clients diverge.

example.title: One round, three clients

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Larger datasets influence the global model more.

example.outcome: a global model learned with few communication rounds.

check.q: Why do clients run multiple local epochs?
check.a: To make more progress per communication round, since communication is the main bottleneck.

the-challenge-non-iid-data-and-client-dr.core: Client data isn't independent and identically distributed: each phone or hospital sees a skewed slice. Local training pulls each client's weights toward its own optimum (client drift), so naive averaging converges slowly or to a worse model.

first_principles.problem: A keyboard model averages updates from users typing different languages and degrades for everyone.
truths: More local steps mean more drift.
Averaging divergent models can cancel progress.
derivation: **Personalise** with local fine-tuning or per-cluster models.

analogy.title: Averaging directions from people in different cities
analogy.story: Each says 'north is that way' from their own position, and the average points nowhere useful.
analogy.breaks: Directions are just wrong; client models each contain real information that better aggregation can recover.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Clients can't wander far from the global model.

check.q: What does FedProx add to the local loss?
check.a: A proximal term penalising distance from the global weights, limiting client drift.

privacy-preserving-ai-differential-priva.core: Model updates can leak training data (gradient inversion, membership inference). Secure Aggregation uses cryptographic masking so the server sees only the sum of updates, never individual ones. Differential Privacy clips each update and adds calibrated noise so no single example measurably changes the result.

first_principles.problem: Researchers reconstruct a patient image from a single client's gradient update.
truths: Masks that cancel in a sum hide individual values.
Noise bounds what any one record reveals (ε budget).
derivation: **Secure aggregation**: pairwise masks cancel when summed.
**DP**: clip update norm, add Gaussian noise.

analogy.title: A secret ballot with fuzzed results
analogy.story: Votes are sealed so only the total is counted, and the total is rounded so no one vote can be inferred.
analogy.breaks: Rounding an election barely matters; DP noise does cost model accuracy.

example.title: DP-FedAvg on a client

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Neither the server nor attackers can isolate one user's contribution.

example.outcome: provable privacy at an accuracy cost.

check.q: What does secure aggregation hide from the server?
check.a: Individual client updates; the server learns only their aggregate sum.
